items.note: The page names the chirp identity for $QF_{\boldsymbol t}$ (with a link) and then derives the cancellation of $R$ and the value $(u*v)/S^2$ from $RF^+_{\boldsymbol s}R=F^+_{\boldsymbol s}$, the commuting of $R$ with pointwise products and the two normalizations. This is the paper's proof of Lemma lem:chirp-permutation (lines 3938-3988). It also gives the conjugation remark for $RF^+_{\boldsymbol s}$.

items.note: Stated with a link to the Bluestein page as assigned: "with $a_{\boldsymbol j}=\exp(-\pi i\sum_i s_ij_i^2/t_i)$, $QF_{\boldsymbol t}u=\overline a\cdot(a*(\overline a\cdot u))/T$". The formula matches eq. (permuted-chirp), but the page does not say that $a$ is periodic of period $t_i$.

The page writes out the substitution $h=ck$, "which runs once over all residues because $c$ is a unit", gets $(F_q^+R_cz)_j=(R_c^{-1}F_q^+z)_j$, and tensors over $R=\bigotimes R_{t_i}$ (each $t_i$ a unit mod $s_i$) to reach $F^+_{\boldsymbol s}R=R^{-1}F^+_{\boldsymbol s}$, hence $RF^+_{\boldsymbol s}R=F^+_{\boldsymbol s}$. This matches paper lines 3953-3962. The worked example with $q=5$, $c=3$ is correct.

The page uses $(RF_{\boldsymbol s}u)\cdot(RF_{\boldsymbol s}v)=R(F_{\boldsymbol s}u\cdot F_{\boldsymbol s}v)$ and the identity just shown, then $F_{\boldsymbol s}(u*v)=S(F_{\boldsymbol s}u)\cdot(F_{\boldsymbol s}v)$ and $F^+_{\boldsymbol s}F_{\boldsymbol s}=I/S$, to get $\frac1SF^+_{\boldsymbol s}F_{\boldsymbol s}(u*v)=\frac{u*v}{S^2}$. This is exactly the paper's chain (lines 3962-3983).
